newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALY'S BAGGIO AWAITS RETURN AGAINST POLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY'S BAGGIO AWAITS RETURN AGAINST POLAND.

text.p: The return of Roberto Baggio could be just one of several new problems facing Poland when they play Italy on Wednesday in their second World Cup qualifying clash in the space of a month.
Poland will be little changed for the group two clash in Naples while Italy have made some major modifications to the side that was held 0-0 in Chorzow.
Baggio, out of the team since 1995, is expected to be a substitute on a night that could take Cesare Maldini's players a huge step closer to the 1998 finals in France.
But a far bigger factor than Baggio for the home team is likely to be provided by the crowd at the San Paolo stadium who will not just be cheering on Italy.
They will be witnessing the return of some of those who contributed to the greatest years in the city's soccer history.
Striker Gianfranco Zola, now with Chelsea in England, was understudy to Diego Maradona when the Argentine took Napoli to their second league title in 1989.
Defender Ciro Ferrara, now with European Cup holders Juventus, was also in that great Napoli team and grew up in the streets of the teeming southern port.
So too did fellow defender Fabio Cannavaro.
Ferrara was booed on his last appearance here with Juventus by some fans who could not forgive his leaving.
The incident brought him a formal apology from Napoli's official fan club and has raised fears of a repeat on Wednesday.
"I hope the fans give us a hand," said Paolo Maldini. "The people of Napoli want to get back into the football that matters and this could be the right moment."
To add to the sense of occasion, Maldini senior played his first international for Italy in Naples 37 years ago.
That match, a 3-0 win against Switzerland, was nowhere near as important as this one.
The match is Italy's last World Cup qualifier until September and one the "Azzurri" must win to maintain their lead over main group rivals England.
Italy currently have 13 points, four clear of second-placed England who have a game in hand.
"We need three points," said Maldini, whose players are unbeaten and have not conceded a goal since he took over from unpopular coach Arrigo Sacchi last last year.
"If we beat Poland then England will be almost on their knees. It means having all the psychological advantage."
England beat Poland 2-1 at Wembley and anything less than three points for Italy could be dangerous -- particularly if England beat the Poles away next month.
Zola, who caused an injury scare last week that led to Baggio being called up, is expected to partner Middlesbrough's returning striker Fabrizio Ravanelli.
Ravanelli missed the last two World Cup qualifiers due to injury and has not partnered Zola up front in a starting line-up since May last year.
The other main attacking option of Christian Vieri evaporated on Monday when the young Juventus star was diagnosed with a tonsil problem and sent home to recuperate.
Atalanta's Filippo Inzaghi, still waiting for his first senior cap despite being the league top scorer this season, is also expected to be on the bench.
Teams:

Italy (probable) - Angelo Peruzzi, Alessandro Costacurta, Paolo Maldini, Fabio Cannavaro, Ciro Ferrara, Angelo Di Livio, Dino Baggio, Demetrio Albertini, Roberto Di Matteo, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Gianfranco Zola
Poland - to be announced
